audit.whatIsWrong: The stage chart reads Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere in both layers, while the paired text says the opposite at five of seven rows: whys[0] 'Tryndamere's crit autos and Bloodlust sustain beat Galio's one-ability Level 1', whys[1] 'the trade is even', whys[2] 'punishes Tryndamere whenever Spinning Slash is down', whys[3] 'let Galio control the lane on his spin cooldowns', whys[4] 'Galio swings the map'.
audit.why: The chart hands Tryndamere levels 2 and 3 — the exact two rows where the text says Galio's full combo comes online and starts punishing — and gives Level 1, which the text says Tryndamere owns, to 'Skill'. At a 50% win rate the honest split is three rows each. A player reading the chart plays this backwards.
audit.corrected: Tryndamere, Skill, Galio, Galio, Galio, Tryndamere, Tryndamere.
sources: scratchpad packet galio.json entry tryndamere (50.0%, 22 games)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers build the Galio window on 'engage when Spinning Slash is down' (whys[2], whys[3], mid, wants.you[0]) and never state its cooldown or that the cooldown shrinks.
audit.why: Spinning Slash is 12/11/10/9/8, but every critical strike reduces its current cooldown by 0.75s, doubled to 1.5s against champions. Once Battle Fury is stacked and he is critting you, the escape comes back in a fraction of the listed time — so 'his dash is down' is a window that closes itself the longer the fight runs. Undying Rage is 120/100/80 for 5 seconds and Bloodlust is 12s.
audit.corrected: Spinning Slash is 12s at rank 1, but each crit on you shaves 1.5s off it — the dash-down window shrinks as the fight goes on, so commit at its start, not into an extended brawl. Undying Rage 120s rank 1 for 5 seconds; Bloodlust 12s.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tryndamere (Spinning Slash 12/11/10/9/8; 'Critical strikes on-hit reduce Spinning Slash's current cooldown by 0.75 seconds, doubled to 1.5 seconds against champions'; Undying Rage 5s, 120/100/80; Bloodlust cooldown 12)

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0] says 'E-punch into his Undying Rage (it catches you mid-dash)', phases[2].why says Justice Punch 'is interruptible and root-able mid-flight', and spikes[3].text says the rage window is one 'your taunt can interrupt and stall'.
audit.why: Undying Rage is a self-buff with no displacement, no immobilise and no interrupt — it cannot catch anything mid-dash. Justice Punch cannot be interrupted once travelling; only an immobilise during cast time stops activation, and Tryndamere has none. And the taunt cannot stop the rage: Undying Rage can be cast while affected by cast-inhibiting crowd control, so a perfectly landed W does not deny it. The entry's three big claims about this ability all point the same wrong way — they tell you a taunt beats the ultimate.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage casts through cast-inhibiting CC, so landing the W taunt does not stop it. It has no CC of its own and cannot touch you mid-dash. The taunt's real job is spending his 5 seconds pointed at you instead of your carry.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tryndamere (Undying Rage 'can be used while affected by cast-inhibiting crowd control', 5 seconds, grants 50/75/100 Fury)
wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] credits Mocking Shout with an 'attack-speed cut' and an unconditional slow.
audit.why: Mocking Shout reduces bonus attack damage by 20/35/50/65/80 — not attack speed — and its slow only applies to enemies facing away from him. Two consequences the entry misses: the AD cut is near-worthless against an AP Galio who buys no bonus AD, and the slow is opt-in, so the real mistake is turning your back to walk out of a trade. Playing it as an attack-speed debuff teaches the wrong response.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout is an 850-range bonus-AD cut on a 14s cooldown, so it barely touches AP Galio — but its slow only lands on targets facing away, so back out of trades facing him or leave with Justice Punch, never by turning and running.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tryndamere (Mocking Shout: 850 range, 14s, reduces bonus attack damage 20/35/50/65/80; 'they become slowed while facing in the opposite direction of Tryndamere')

audit.why: The entry already says the shield is 'heavily amplified against MAGIC' and that his physical crits go through it — that is right, and the numbers back it: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% but physical only 12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%. The edits below attach the number so the player knows how small the cushion is.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, even though the full layer's Itemization line already carries 'Oblivion Orb early'.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for this pairing via Bloodlust. Bloodlust heals 30/40/50/60/70 plus 0.5-2.3 per Fury consumed on a 12-second cooldown, and a full Fury bar makes that the difference between a won trade and a reset one. The reader of the content page gets no anti-heal cue at all.
audit.corrected: Bloodlust is a 12-second heal that scales with the Fury he has banked — Grievous Wounds before your second item is what stops him resetting every trade you win.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer gives the range Galio pokes from.
audit.why: Winds of War is 825 against a 650 Spinning Slash and a melee auto. content.early says 'last-hit from max range with the outer windblasts' without the number, so the player cannot tell whether he is safe from the spin.
audit.corrected: Winds of War is 825; Spinning Slash reaches 650. Poke from beyond 650 and the spin cannot answer without committing.

audit.why: The packet flags "Justice Punch's", "Mocking Shout's" and "Use Hero's Entrance" as probable wrong ability names. All three are false positives from the near-miss matcher — the names are correct; only the mechanic attached to Mocking Shout was wrong, which is handled above.
50.0% over 22 games; TRICKY at 7.5/10 with an 8.5/10 carry threat is defensible against a champion who cannot be killed through his ultimate. Small sample, so I did not move the rating.

edits.before: Tryndamere wins the opening — his crit autos and Bloodlust sustain shrug off Galio's single ability at Level 1, so concede the first wave and last-hit from max range with the outer windblasts of Winds of War instead of stepping into auto range. Don't expect Shield of Durand to bail you out of a straight trade: its damage reduction is heavily amplified against MAGIC, and Tryndamere deals pure physical crit, so the shield is at its weakest exactly here. The lane only turns at 3 once Justice Punch and the W-taunt are both online. Never start a trade while his Fury bar is near full — that is when his crits hurt most.
edits.after: Tryndamere wins the opening — his crit autos and Bloodlust sustain shrug off Galio's single ability at Level 1, so concede the first wave and last-hit with the outer windblasts of Winds of War at 825, well outside his 650 spin. Don't expect Shield of Durand to bail you out of a straight trade: it cuts magic damage 25% at rank 1 but physical only 12.5%, and Tryndamere is pure physical crit, so the shield is at its weakest exactly here. The lane only turns at 3 once Justice Punch and the W-taunt are both online. Never start a trade while his Fury bar is near full — that is when his crits hurt most.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 are Galio's window: poke with Q's center column and the empowered Colossal Smash auto, then punish with a pre-charged Shield of Durand taunt into Justice Punch whenever Spinning Slash is on cooldown — the dash is his only way off you, so engage when it's down. At 6 the real lane is the other two: Hero's Entrance lets you shove and flag a sidelane 2v1, which matters far more than the coinflip duel here. Bait his Mocking Shout, hold E to interrupt his commit, and remember the shield does little against his physical crits even when fully channeled.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 5 are Galio's window: poke with Q's center column and the empowered Colossal Smash auto, then punish with a pre-charged Shield of Durand taunt into Justice Punch while Spinning Slash is down — but every crit he lands shaves 1.5 seconds off that 12-second dash, so open at full and never grind. At 6 the real lane is the other two: Hero's Entrance lets you shove and flag a sidelane 2v1, which matters far more than the coinflip duel. Leave trades facing him — Mocking Shout only slows targets who turn their backs — and remember the shield stops just 12.5% of his crits.

notes: Galio facts verified at wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio and reused across this slice: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% and physical exactly half that (12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%); its passive is a magic shield of 7.5/9/10.5/12/13.5% max health restoring after 12/10/8s (by level) out of combat; the taunt lands on release, radius 175-350 and 0.5-1.5s duration scaled by channel time. Justice Punch knocks up 0.75s, cannot be interrupted mid-travel (only an immobilise during cast time stops it), is disabled while Grounded, and the charge halts on terrain or champions. Winds of War is 825 range, tornado 2s, no slow; windblasts blockable individually by Wind Wall / Unbreakable, spell shield eats the gusts but not the tornado. Hero's Entrance channels 2.75s, CC-immune after 1.25s, grants allies the Shield of Durand magic shield for 5s. Colossal Smash is a 5s empowered auto (reduced 3s per ability hit on a champion), 250 radius, scaling with 60% bonus magic resist. Galio kit-file flag misfires: E is tagged 'terrain' (it creates none) and lacks 'knockup' despite Riot's description saying 'knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters' — description trusted. NOT verified and therefore left as a general argument rather than a stated fact: whether Grievous Wounds reduces Bloodlust's healing (the wiki page does not state it).
